LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines sources for two architectures (x86_64 and aarch64), fetching prebuilt binary tarballs from the project's GitHub releases page using HTTPS. The URLs are constructed from variables referencing the maintainer's declared GitHub repository (`_gitauthor=mehranzand`, `_gitname=repofleet`), and point to versioned release assets. These are standard, expected practices for a binary package in the AUR.

The `pkgver` is hardcoded as `0.7.5`, so no dynamic version fetching occurs. There is no `pkgver()` function, and no command substitution or side-effecting expressions in the global scope. The only executed code during sourcing is simple variable assignment, array definition, and string interpolation — all inert and safe operations.

The sources are verified with provided sha256sums, so even though checksum verification is not required for this gate, their presence further reduces risk. No network requests, file operations, or code execution occur outside of the declared source downloads when sourcing the PKGBUILD or running `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. There is no use of `eval`, `curl|bash`, or other dangerous patterns in the top-level scope.

Thus, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is safe: it will only download the specified release binaries and parse the PKGBUILD without executing any untrusted code.
</details>
<summary>
No dangerous code in top-level scope; safe sourcing
</summary>
</security_assessment>
